checked_decisions.finding: Text ids 114-118 form one exchange: Saotome (elderly 'oran' speech, 'oroka' echoed in 2216/2219) - retort - Saotome to a singular 'omae'. 'Earth's last day' (chikyuu) here is kept distinct from 'the world's last day' (sekai) of 2214/2271, as in the source. No connective links 2215 to 2214.
Translator doubt on the number of 'kan': plural 'ships' accepted. 2209 'kakukan' and 2278 'kakukan ga sen'iki wo toppa' show several ships advance (Tower, Nadesico and Gekko each have damage lines).
'kyoten' = 'base' accepted; it is already the corpus form in reviewed rows 993-1032 and 1603-1633 (capture a base).
Generic operator rows; 'particle field' matches reviewed rows 1267-1307. Translated faithfully whether or not used in this mission.
Alternative ship-damage / ship-loss lines; no speaker or gender asserted. 2252-2253 kept subjectless. 2258 'Captain' per orchestrator decision.
'Genki' matches the alias in character_names_021; 'daughter' only where the source says musume (2270, 2272, 2276, 2281), 'child' where it says wagako (2266, 2267, 2269).
'oyaji' = 'Dad' accepted. 2277 is unambiguously Kei's; 2273 is addressed to the same person, who answers in 2274-2276.
Supplied 'you' accepted: 2276 (same window, no <ed()> between) has 'omae'.
Unnamed manned unit not named; 2288 passive 'seen' keeps the unstated observer open. 'Saint Cruz' matches glossary.
Zentradi and Getter Rays spellings match glossary/corpus.

uncertainties.issue: (Row belongs to batch_02135, not edited.) 'Saotome-me...' plus plain '...kuratta hazu da' reads as a mutter about Saotome in the third person, which Saotome then answers theatrically in 2213 ('I told you I would not die'). The current 'Saotome, damn you... should have hit you head-on' asserts direct address. Suggested ambiguity-keeping form: 'Damn that Saotome... The Deuteron Missile should have been a direct hit.'

2213-2214 (ids 112-113) close with <ed()> and answer 2212; 2215 opens a new window with <op()> and starts the separate exchange 114-118. Same speaker (Saotome) but separate exchanges, possibly separate triggers. The apparent contradiction (witness the world's last day vs avert Earth's last day) is in the source and is preserved.
'we fought' supplies a subject the source omits (izen ni tatakatta); harmless because the speaker is an allied pilot, left as is.
Echo of Saotome's 'wagako'. 'My child...?' works as a quoted echo; if the speaker is a third party 'His child...?' would be more natural. Speaker untagged, left.

'ano kitai' rendered singular ('that machine', 'It may have'); the recap in 2374 says 'ano mujinki', rendered plural 'Those unmanned units'. Number is not recoverable from the source; the two rows disagree in English only.
Whose escort units (escort sent to the ships' rear / escort wiped out) is not stated; elsewhere 'goei butai' is also the enemy force guarding a base (1270). Kept neutral.
